User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the Dotly application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user entity.

preferredCauses.description: List of causes the user is interested in supporting.

preferredAssociations.description: List of association IDs the user is interested in supporting.

donationMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to donations based on user income.

isAssociation.description: Flag indicating if the user represents an association.

Association.title: Association
Association.description: Represents an association registered on the Dotly application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the association entity.

contactEmail.description: Contact email address of the association.

contactPhoneNumber.description: Contact phone number of the association.

rnaNumber.description: RNA (Répertoire National des Associations) number of the association.

description.description: Description of the association's activities and mission.

currentMissions.description: Current missions the association is trying to fund.

taxReceiptEligible.description: Indicates if the association is eligible to issue tax receipts.

Donation.title: Donation
Donation.description: Represents a single donation made by a user to an association.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made the donation. (Relationship: User 1:N Donation)

associationId.description: Reference to the Association that received the donation. (Relationship: Association 1:N Donation)

amount.description: Amount of the donation in euros.

transactionDate.description: Date and time when the donation was processed.

roundedUpAmount.description: The amount the transaction was rounded up to.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to address the 'Missing or insufficient permissions' error by ensuring authorization independence and secure data access.  The error occurred because the user was attempting to `list` all documents in the `donations` collection, which is not allowed in this structure. `Donations` are stored within user-specific subcollections, ensuring users can only list *their* donations. This design avoids the security risks of allowing general collection listing.

Key structural choices:

1.  **Authorization Independence:** The structure uses path-based ownership for donations (`/users/{userId}/donations/{donationId}`). This eliminates the need for `get()` calls in security rules to check the donor's identity, since the `userId` is embedded in the path. No denormalization is required because authorization is implicit in the path.

2.  **Structural Segregation:**  User data, association data, and donation data are stored in separate collections to enforce distinct security policies.  Donations are further segregated as subcollections under the respective user's document.

3. **User and Association Separation:** User and association data are strictly segregated. There is no mixing of data related to users or associations in the same collection or document. This segregation allows for distinct security rules for users and associations.

4.  **QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
    *   Listing donations is restricted to the donations owned by the user. Therefore, a user can list donations under `/users/{userId}/donations`, but not donations of other users. Associations should not be able to list donations. This is a critical security feature.

This design promotes security and scalability by enforcing clear ownership and limiting access to data based on the user's identity.
